name: Rich text, numbered sections
description: A long guide split into sections, each with a large number that stays in view beside its text.

fields.name: title
fields.label: Title
fields.default: Five rules for interviews people want to join

fields.name: lead
fields.label: Lead paragraph
fields.default: The guidelines our own team follows, from the first invite to the thank-you note.

default.heading: Ask for thirty minutes, not an hour
default.body: Short calls fill faster and keep everyone focused. If a conversation is going well, people are happy to stay a few extra minutes.

default.heading: Say what happens to the recording
default.body: Explain who will hear it, how long it is kept and how to ask for it to be deleted. Put it in the invite, then say it again at the start of the call.

default.heading: Talk about their week, not your product
default.body:
Spend the first five minutes on their role and routine. The useful stories come from real situations, not opinions about features.

  • “Walk me through yesterday.”
  • “When did that last happen?”

default.heading: Bring someone to take notes
default.body: A second person tags highlights live, so you can listen properly and nobody rewatches the call later.

default.heading: Follow up within a week
default.body: Send a thank-you and one sentence on what you changed because of them. It is the best recruiting tool you have.
